DEST.name: Ayia Napa
DEST.line: Cape Greco, sea caves and some of the island's best-known beaches.
DEST.hero: Cape Greco cliffs above turquoise water
glance: Where
The south-east corner of the island, east of Larnaca.
Known for
Beaches, Cape Greco, the sea caves, waterparks and nightlife.
Getting oriented
The town centre and monastery sit just inland from the harbour, with beaches spread east and west.
plan: Getting there
Larnaca International Airport is the nearest airport.
Taxis
Urban taxis use the meter. Day tariff from €3.80 plus €0.95 per km.
Buses
Routes and fares to be added.
Seasons
Summer is peak season. Spring and autumn are warm and quieter.

DEST.name: Protaras & Eastern Villages
DEST.line: Calm sandy bays, easy family days and strawberry fields inland.
DEST.hero: Fig Tree Bay on a calm morning
glance: Where
The east coast, just north of Cape Greco, beside Paralimni.
Known for
Fig Tree Bay, sheltered coves, family holidays and Deryneia strawberries.
Getting oriented
Protaras is the resort strip on the coast. Paralimni and Deryneia are the working towns just inland.
plan: Getting there
Larnaca International Airport is the nearest airport.
Taxis
Urban taxis use the meter. Day tariff from €3.80 plus €0.95 per km.
Buses
Routes and fares to be added.
Seasons
Summer is peak season. Deryneia's strawberry season is in spring.

DEST.name: Paphos
DEST.line: Mosaics, myths and the rock where Aphrodite rose from the sea.
glance: Where
The west coast of the island.
Known for
Mosaics, the Tombs of the Kings, the harbour, Aphrodite's Rock and nearby wineries.
Getting oriented
Kato Paphos is the harbour and archaeology area by the sea. The old town, Ktima, sits on the hill above.
plan: Getting there
Paphos International Airport is in this region.
Taxis
Urban taxis use the meter. Day tariff from €3.80 plus €0.95 per km.
Buses
Routes and fares to be added.
Seasons
Summer is peak season. Spring and autumn suit the archaeological sites.

DEST.name: Polis, Latchi & Akamas
DEST.line: Wild coast, clear water and walks without crowds.

DEST.name: Larnaca & Villages
DEST.line: A slow seafront, old crafts and some of the island's oldest stories.
DEST.hero: Larnaca seafront and the hills behind
glance: Where
The south-east coast, with villages inland towards the Troodos foothills.
Known for
The seafront, religious heritage, the Salt Lake, Lefkara lace and silver.
Getting oriented
Larnaca International Airport sits on the edge of town, close to the Salt Lake.
plan: Getting there
Larnaca International Airport is in this region.
Taxis
Urban taxis use the meter. Day tariff from €3.80 plus €0.95 per km.
Buses
Routes and fares to be added.
Seasons
Summer is hot. Spring, autumn and winter suit village walks and the Salt Lake.

DEST.name: Nicosia
DEST.line: Courtyards, museums and a capital that stays up late.

DEST.name: Troodos & Mountain Villages
DEST.line: Pine air, stone villages and painted churches.

cape-greco.name: Cape Greco
cape-greco.intro: Sea cliffs, caves and clear turquoise water at the island's south-east tip.
cape-greco.why: Walk the headland at sunrise, look down into water so clear you can see the rocks below, and follow the coast path to the sea caves.
features: Coastal walking trails across the headland.
The small chapel of Agioi Anargyroi above the sea.
Views along the coast towards Ayia Napa and Protaras.
practical: Cliff edges are unfenced in places. Stay on the paths.
Not yet verified. Paths are rocky.

sources.t: Ayia Napa, Protaras and eastern-region tourism

sea-caves.name: Ayia Napa Sea Caves
sea-caves.intro: Caves carved into the cliffs between Ayia Napa and Cape Greco.
sea-caves.why: Best seen from a boat or from the clifftop at golden hour, when the rock glows and the water turns deep blue.
features: Sea caves you can see from the clifftop or by boat.
Part of the Cape Greco coastline.
The Love Bridge, a natural rock arch, is closer to town, east of the harbour.
practical: Cliff edges are unfenced. Jumping from the rocks is dangerous.
Operators to be added once verified.

sources.t: Ayia Napa, Protaras and eastern-region tourism

nissi.name: Nissi Beach
nissi.intro: A wide sandy bay with a small islet you can wade to when the sea is calm.
nissi.why: Soft sand, shallow water and a lively summer atmosphere, a short walk from town.
features: Shallow, sandy water near the shore.
A small islet linked by a sandbar in calm seas.

sources.t: Ayia Napa, Protaras and eastern-region tourism

makronissos.name: Makronissos Beach
makronissos.intro: Sandy coves west of Ayia Napa, with ancient rock-cut tombs on the headland nearby.
makronissos.why: A calmer alternative to the busiest beaches, with a small piece of history a few minutes' walk away.
features: Sheltered sandy coves.
Ancient rock-cut tombs nearby.

sources.t: Ayia Napa, Protaras and eastern-region tourism

napa-monastery.name: Ayia Napa Monastery
napa-monastery.intro: A Venetian-era monastery with a quiet courtyard in the middle of town.
napa-monastery.why: Step out of the summer bustle into shade and stone, right in the centre of town.
features: Built during Venetian rule, around 1500.
Part of the church is carved into the rock.
A courtyard with a central fountain.

sources.t: Ayia Napa, Protaras and eastern-region tourism

waterworld.name: WaterWorld Waterpark
waterworld.intro: A big waterpark themed on Greek mythology, just outside Ayia Napa.
waterworld.why: A full day out for kids and teenagers, with slides and pools built around the old myths.
features: Rides themed on Greek mythology.
Pools for younger children.
practical: Listed as open April to October. Check before you go.

sources.t: Ayia Napa, Protaras and eastern-region tourism

fig-tree-bay.name: Fig Tree Bay
fig-tree-bay.intro: A sandy bay with a small islet a short swim from the shore.
fig-tree-bay.why: Clear, calm water and soft sand. It's the beach most people picture when they think of Protaras.
features: A small islet you can swim out to.
Calm water on most summer days.

sources.t: Ayia Napa, Protaras and eastern-region tourism

konnos.name: Konnos Bay
konnos.intro: A sheltered cove below pine-covered slopes, between Protaras and Cape Greco.
konnos.why: Turquoise water in a small, protected bay. Go early in summer, it fills up.
features: Sheltered water, good for a calm swim.
Close to the Cape Greco walking trails.
practical: Not yet verified. The road down is steep.

sources.t: Ayia Napa, Protaras and eastern-region tourism

profitis-ilias.name: Profitis Ilias Chapel
profitis-ilias.intro: A small chapel on a rock above Protaras, with views along the coast.
profitis-ilias.why: Climb the steps at sunset for one of the best views on the east coast.
features: Steps up to the chapel.
Wide views over Protaras and the sea.

sources.t: Ayia Napa, Protaras and eastern-region tourism

deryneia.name: Deryneia
deryneia.intro: A farming town just inland, known for its strawberries.
deryneia.why: Come in spring for the strawberry season and a look at the island's eastern farmland.
features: Strawberry fields and local produce.
A working town, away from the resort strip.

sources.t: Ayia Napa, Protaras and eastern-region tourism

aphrodite-rock.name: Aphrodite's Rock
aphrodite-rock.intro: The sea stack where, the legend goes, Aphrodite rose from the foam.
aphrodite-rock.why: Stop on the coast road between Paphos and Limassol for the view, the waves and the story that made Cyprus the island of love.
features: Also called Petra tou Romiou.
Pebble beach and dramatic rocks.
aphrodite-rock.legend: Greek myth says Aphrodite, goddess of love, was born from the sea foam here. The local name, Petra tou Romiou, comes from a different story about the Byzantine hero Digenis.
practical: Not yet verified. Waves and currents can be strong.

kato-paphos.name: Kato Paphos Archaeological Park
kato-paphos.intro: Roman villas by the sea, with some of the finest floor mosaics in the Mediterranean.
kato-paphos.why: Walk among the ruins of ancient Nea Paphos and see mythological scenes laid in stone, right beside the harbour.
features: Part of the Paphos UNESCO World Heritage Site, inscribed in 1980.
Mosaic floors in the Roman villas.
A short walk from Paphos harbour.
practical: Not yet verified. Much of the site is open ground.
Early morning or late afternoon in summer, for shade and softer light.

tombs-kings.name: Tombs of the Kings
tombs-kings.intro: Underground tombs cut into the rock above the sea, with columned courtyards you can walk down into.
tombs-kings.why: Despite the name, no kings were buried here. The tombs belonged to Paphian aristocrats and high officials, and many date from the 4th century BC.
features: Part of the Paphos UNESCO World Heritage Site.
Rock-cut chambers and courtyards with columns.
Open, coastal setting north of the harbour.
practical: Not yet verified. Steps lead down into the tombs.

paphos-castle.name: Paphos Harbour and Castle
paphos-castle.intro: A small stone fort at the end of the harbour, with fishing boats and seafront cafés all around.
paphos-castle.why: The easiest place to start in Paphos. Walk the harbour front at sunset, then eat by the water.
features: Stone fort at the harbour entrance.
Seafront promenade with cafés and restaurants.
practical: Not yet verified for the fort.

lefkara.name: Lefkara
lefkara.intro: A hill village of honey-coloured stone, known for lace and silver made by hand.
lefkara.why: Come for the craft. Lefkara's lace, called lefkaritika, has been made here for generations, and lace and silver shops line the village lanes.
features: Lefkaritika lace, inscribed on UNESCO's list of Intangible Cultural Heritage in 2009.
A long tradition of silverwork and filigree.
Narrow lanes and stone houses that reward a slow walk.
lefkara.legend: Local legend says Leonardo da Vinci visited in 1481 and took a lace altar cloth back to Milan Cathedral. It's a much-loved story, but it isn't documented history.
practical: Open village. Shop hours vary and are not yet verified.
No entry fee for the village itself.
Not yet verified. Some lanes are steep.
Mornings, before the midday heat in summer.

choirokoitia.name: Choirokoitia
choirokoitia.intro: A Neolithic village on a hillside, with reconstructed round houses you can step inside.
choirokoitia.why: It's one of the most important prehistoric sites in the eastern Mediterranean, and the reconstructed round houses make it easy for kids to picture daily life.
features: UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1998.
Reconstructed stone round houses near the entrance.
Hillside paths with views across the valley.
practical: Not yet verified. Check before you go.
Not yet verified. The site is on a slope.

salt-lake.name: Larnaca Salt Lake
salt-lake.intro: A wide salt lake on the edge of town, at its best in winter when it fills with water.
salt-lake.why: A flat, easy walk with big skies, right beside the city. In winter, flamingos often stop here, though numbers change from year to year.
features: Seasonal wildlife. Flamingos are common in winter but never guaranteed.
Hala Sultan Tekke sits on its western shore.
Flat ground, good for an easy family walk.
practical: The lake is often dry in late summer.

hala-sultan.name: Hala Sultan Tekke
hala-sultan.intro: An Ottoman-era mosque among palms on the shore of the Salt Lake.
hala-sultan.why: One of the island's most important Muslim sites, in a calm, green setting by the water.
features: Mosque complex surrounded by gardens and palms.
Views across the Salt Lake.
practical: Modest dress expected when visiting the mosque.

st-lazarus.name: Church of Saint Lazarus
st-lazarus.intro: A stone church in the heart of old Larnaca, dedicated to Saint Lazarus.
st-lazarus.why: The church anchors the old town. Walk the surrounding streets for cafés, small shops and the seafront a few minutes away.
features: Built in the late 9th or early 10th century over the tomb of Saint Lazarus.
A gilded, carved wooden iconostasis from the 1770s.
Surrounded by the old town's walkable streets.
practical: Shoulders and knees covered inside the church.

sources.t: Wikipedia: Church of Saint Lazarus, Larnaca

finikoudes.name: Finikoudes
finikoudes.intro: Larnaca's palm-lined seafront, with a sandy town beach and cafés along the front.
finikoudes.why: Easy, central and lively in the evening. Swim in the morning, walk the promenade at sunset.
features: Sandy town beach next to the promenade.
Cafés and restaurants along the seafront.

silver-sample.name: [Lefkara silver workshop]
silver-sample.line: Family workshop making filigree silver by hand.
